subject: illustrated_tree

subject: moens
evidence: Mr. Moens visited Ceylon in September 1880, and it is to him that I am indebted for having first pointed out to me that the plant had good definite characters.

subject: christie
evidence: The plant which Dr. Trimen figured was one of those raised from McIvor's seed by me, and planted on Mahanilu by Mr. Agar, and its descent from Ledger's original seed is undoubted.
interpretation_note: Christie’s asserted provenance; not independently demonstrated chain of custody.

subject: agar
evidence: planted on Mahanilu by Mr. Agar

subject: illustrated_tree
evidence: It was one of several Mr. Moens saw in flower at Mahanillu estate, Dr. Trimen was with Mr. Moens, and both agreed the trees were true Ledgerianas.

subject: campbell
evidence: The bark of some of these trees was sent home by Mr. Campbell for analysis to Mr. Howard,
interpretation_note: From some trees in group; do not substitute illustrated tree as sample source.

subject: howard
evidence: who pronounced it to be Ledgeriana bark, giving 7 per cent of pure quinine (equal I believe to 9 of sulphate) and only a trace of other alkaloids.
interpretation_note: Historical reported assay, with narrator’s qualified conversion; not independently validated measurement.

subject: agar
evidence: I have also in my possession the bark from the tree itself, but taken when it was dying.

subject: howard
evidence: I find that I am credited with having created a new species of Cinchona, the "*C. pubescens* How."
interpretation_note: Following sentences explicitly reject this attribution; preserve rejected name as historical usage.

subject: markham
evidence: Mr. Clements Markham's mistake in putting it as a hybrid of *Calisaya* and *Officialis* was commented on.
interpretation_note: Editorial attribution of an error; not a fresh independent botanical determination.

subject: markham
date_as_stated: event date not specified in excerpt
evidence: The first consignment of plants was collected and brought to Bombay by Mr. Clements R. Markham. As the plants were not quite healthy they were all sent to Neilgherry instead of a few being sent here as was first intended.
interpretation_note: Publication 1943; Markham brought plants to Bombay, onward consignment sent to Nilgiris. Does not establish that he accompanied the onward leg.
